review.exclusion: Denied attempts are blocked per-attempt: when validate_file_path/validate_directory_path reject (startswith fails, missing path, not-a-directory), read_file/list_directory convert ValueError/FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError into ModelRetry (codebase_tools.py:91-92,114-115) and no open()/listdir executes on that attempt; the SDK Tool returns RetryPromptPart to the model (tools.py:383-398) and aborts the run with UnexpectedModelBehavior on the second rejection. This blocking does not extend to sibling-prefix paths because containment is the purely lexical str.startswith(normpath(project_dir)) test (config.py:133-138,157-158), under which '<project_dir>-sibling/...' passes while lying outside the project directory, so no exclusion can be established.
review.forbidden_condition: A codebase tool touches a path outside the configured project directory: read_file opens and reads file content, or list_directory lists entries via os.listdir, for a path not within project_dir (obligation: read/list only paths within the configured project directory).
missing_evidence: Symlink/hardlink and TOCTOU routes were not analyzed: normpath is purely lexical while os.path.exists/open follow symlinks, and the admission scope explicitly excluded symlink-correctness decisions; such an additional out-of-project route would require filesystem state not established here.

No live run is observed; that the decision model emits a sibling-path read_file call is a structurally legal tool-call output under the declared interface (untrusted, prompt-obeying behavior not assumed), not an observed completion.

Full transitive dependency solving and wheel/platform installation for the alternative pip profile were not performed (per reference_selection.critical_unknowns); SDK/API compatibility is asserted from the supplied 0.1.11 sources only.

Other reading/listing tools sharing the same lexical validators (find_in_files recursion, find_symbol_references via _search_files, get_import_tree, get_stack_frame_context) were not exhaustively traced; only the contract's named protected operations read_file and list_directory were witness-traced.

trace.event: analyze command: --project-dir is a required, caller-configurable option; the run uses project_dir=/workspace/project (an existing directory).
CodebaseContext(project_dir=cli_args.project_dir) is constructed; AbsolutePath keeps the absolute string '/workspace/project'.
StackTraceAgent.__init__ creates Agent[CodebaseContext,str](output_type=str, deps_type=CodebaseContext, model_settings=GeminiModelSettings(...)) and calls register_tools(self.agent, max_retries=3).

Bare @agent.tool registers Tool(func=read_file, name='read_file') and returns func, so the retry_on_error wrapper only rebinds the local name; the SDK Tool object holds the raw coroutine with the guard call.
agent.iter(initial_prompt, deps=project_fs) drives the graph; CallToolsNode processes the model response.

Model response contains ToolCallPart(tool_name='read_file', args={'file_path': '/workspace/project-notes/config.py'}) — an input choice that is structurally legal under the registered tool schema (file_path: str); no source-level restriction constrains the string value.
process_function_tools: function_tools.get('read_file') matches the registered Tool and the call is queued in calls_to_run.
asyncio.create_task(tool.run(call, run_context, ctx.deps.tracer)) dispatches the tool call.
Tool._run validates the JSON args against the tool schema and awaits function(ctx, file_path='/workspace/project-notes/config.py') — the raw read_file captured at registration.
read_file calls ctx.deps.validate_file_path('/workspace/project-notes/config.py').

Path is already absolute; both strings are normpath'd; the containment test is the plain string predicate file_path.startswith(project_dir), and '/workspace/project-notes/config.py'.startswith('/workspace/project') is True, so no ValueError is raised even though the path lies outside the configured project directory.
os.path.exists passes for the existing sibling file and the validator returns the out-of-project abs_path unchanged.
open(abs_path,'r',encoding='utf-8') succeeds on the sibling file and f.read() returns its contents: the protected read commits on the same attempt that realizes the forbidden out-of-project state.
No ModelRetry occurs on this attempt; Tool._run returns ToolReturnPart(content=...) and the out-of-project file contents flow back into the run.
